title: Sponge City fact cards
purpose: Short, sourced facts that explain each sponge-city intervention or action, for visual explainers. Every fact carries exactly one evidence class; numbers are quoted as their source states them, with the caveat that matters.

evidence.basel-data: Computed by us from Basel open data; method and dataset named; reproducible with docs/pilots/
evidence.official: Stated by an authority (Basel-Stadt or another city or canton)
evidence.research: From a cited study or guideline; the setting may not be Basel
evidence.inference: Our own reasoning from the facts above; not measured

visuals.bars: two or more bars to compare
visuals.share: part of a whole (stacked bar, 100 squares)
visuals.map: points or areas on the Basel map

context.claim: 45 % of Basel-Stadt's ground is sealed: 16.6 % buildings and 28.5 % paved surfaces. Roads alone cover 9.5 %, sidewalks 4.2 %.
context.method: Area of all land-cover polygons by class (36.6 km² total).
context.caveat: Planted areas include gardens and parks; 'unsealed' is not the same as 'absorbs well' (see compaction).

context.claim: Basel-Binningen had 8.8 hot days (≥ 30 °C) a year in 1961–1990, 14.3 in 1991–2020, and 21.9 in 2015–2024.
context.method: Days with daily maximum ≥ 30 °C, averaged per period (complete years only).

context.claim: Days with 20 mm of rain or more did not become more frequent in Basel's daily record (5.4 a year in 1961–1990, 6.2 in 1991–2020, 5.2 in 2015–2024). The wettest day on record is 25 May 1872 with 94.8 mm; 26 July 1991 had 85 mm.
context.method: Days with daily precipitation ≥ 20 mm per period; ranking of daily totals since 1864.
context.caveat: Cloudbursts last minutes to hours; daily totals hide them. Sub-hourly data (MeteoSwiss 10-minute series) is needed for that question.

context.claim: Tree crowns cover about 25 % of the canton (2021 LiDAR evaluation), which has changed only marginally over the past ten years.
63 % of Basel's street length (194 km) carries little enough traffic to be rated suitable for sponge measures; 10 % (30 km) needs checking and 27 % (81 km) is not suitable.
context.method: Sum of segment lengths per suitability class of the canton's model (≤ 2,000 vehicles/day suitable, ≥ 4,000 not suitable).
context.caveat: Traffic is one criterion; utilities, groundwater and space are not in this rating.

interventions.name: Keep the old trees
interventions.what: A mature tree cannot be replaced by a young one for decades. Protecting and caring for existing trees is the cheapest sponge measure.

facts.claim: Around Basel's street trees, the median canopy within 8 m grows with time at the site: about 20 m² for trees there up to 12 years, 46 m² at 13–25 years, 78 m² at 26–50, 118 m² at 51–80 and 138 m² for trees there more than 80 years.
facts.method: Canopy pixels within 8 m of each of 12,504 street trees, grouped by years at site (docs/pilots/tree_pit_canopy.py).
facts.caveat: The 8 m circle can include neighbouring crowns; years at site is not tree age.

facts.claim: In Santa Monica, a small young tree intercepted 15 % of the rain falling on it, a mature tree up to 66 %.

source.label: Xiao & McPherson, rainfall interception by Santa Monica's urban forest

facts.caveat: Californian climate and species; interception is highest in small summer storms.

facts.claim: The same large plane tree intercepted about 15 % of a 22 mm winter storm (no leaves) but about 80 % of a 20 mm summer storm.

source.label: Xiao & McPherson, rainfall interception by Santa Monica's urban forest

facts.claim: Basel renews about 1 % of its tree stock a year; the tree cadastre lists over 28,000 trees, about 2,000 more than ten years ago.
≈ Felling one old street tree removes canopy that a new tree needs several decades to rebuild.
facts.caveat: Growth depends on species and root space.

interventions.name: Give trees more root space
interventions.what: Enlarge the planted area and the soil volume around a street tree, so roots get water and air.

facts.claim: 73 % of Basel's street trees (9,132 of 12,504) stand in surfaces the official survey maps as sealed: their pit is too small to be mapped. The rest stand in mapped planting strips (median 371 m²).
facts.method: Tree point inside sealed vs planted land-cover polygon.
facts.caveat: An enlarged pit still below the mapping threshold counts as sealed.

facts.claim: Bern's guidance sets a target root space of 36 m³ per street tree, with pits at least 1 m deep (1.5 m where needed).

source.label: Stadt Bern: Arbeitshilfe Wurzelraum für Strassenbäume

facts.claim: Small-leaved limes in Munich cooled their surroundings with up to 2.3 kW (sap flow up to 8 litres an hour); on narrow paved squares with small tree pits the cooling was at least 20 % lower than in open green squares.

source.label: TU München press release, 14 Sept 2016 (Rahman et al.)

facts.claim: Basel enlarged the tree pits of the Engelgasse and replanted 50 young trees, because the old pits gave too little root space.

interventions.name: Tree trench (sponge root bed)
interventions.what: A connected bed of load-bearing substrate under the pavement: roots grow in it, and runoff from the street is led into it.

facts.claim: The Stockholm method fills a large pit with coarse stones that carry the pavement; the gaps hold compost and biochar, roots, air and water. Trees grow larger and the bed takes street runoff.

source.label: Vermont Urban & Community Forestry: Using the Stockholm planting method

facts.claim: Basel tests sponge-city elements in the new VoltaNord streets and monitors them scientifically for five years (CHF 280,000 approved).
ZHAW develops vegetation building blocks with draining, resource-saving substrates for three Basel streets: Therwilerstrasse, Lysbüchelstrasse and Weinlagerstrasse.

interventions.name: Water the young trees
interventions.what: Newly planted trees need regular water for their first years, especially in hot, dry summers.

facts.claim: The Woodland Trust advises about 50 litres a week for newly planted street trees in summer, for the first three years. Richmond (London) waters with about 10 litres every two days and plans 19 contractor visits a year for the first three years.

source.label: Woodland Trust press release, June 2023; London Borough of Richmond: tree watering

facts.claim: A 2009 survey cited by the Woodland Trust found that 30 % of newly planted street trees die in their first years, often up to 50 %.
facts.caveat: UK figure from a survey cited by an NGO; causes vary, dry weather is one.

facts.claim: ≈ With hot days in Basel up from about 9 a year (1961–1990) to about 22 (2015–2024), the first summers are getting harder for new trees.

interventions.name: Unseal
interventions.what: Remove asphalt or concrete where it is not needed and replace it with soil and planting.

facts.claim: 45 % of Basel-Stadt's ground is sealed; roads alone are 347 ha, sidewalks 153 ha.
facts.method: Area of all land-cover polygons by class (36.6 km² total), see context fact basel-sealed.

facts.claim: In Manchester, grass lowered maximum surface temperatures by up to 24 °C compared with concrete; tree shade by up to 19 °C, and shade cut the temperature people feel (globe temperature) by 5–7 °C.

source.label: Armson, Stringer & Ennos (2012), Urban Forestry & Urban Greening

facts.claim: Compaction by construction cut soil infiltration by 70–99 % in a Florida study; without deliberate restoration, recovery can take decades.

source.label: Gregor et al., Journal of Soil and Water Conservation (compaction study)

facts.caveat: Sandy Florida soils; the point is that unsealing alone is not enough, the soil must be loosened.

facts.claim: At Sevogelstrasse, about 1,000 m² of asphalt will be unsealed and about 600 m² become green space, with 32 new trees (from spring 2026).

interventions.name: Permeable parking
interventions.what: Parking bays paved with grass-joint stones or open joints let rain soak in where cars stand.

facts.claim: Sevogelstrasse gets 14 parking bays with grass-joint stones; parking there goes from 36 to 19 spaces.
Studies report the infiltration capacity of permeable pavements falling by 63–100 % over time as joints clog; with regular cleaning, systems still performed after eight years.

source.label: Villanova Urban Stormwater Partnership: permeable pavement

facts.caveat: Figures compiled from several studies; maintenance makes the difference.

facts.claim: Basel tested surfaces for depaved parking spaces in 2022.

interventions.name: Rain garden
interventions.what: A shallow planted hollow that collects runoff from nearby paving and lets it soak in or evaporate.

facts.claim: Across 20 US studies, bioretention retained, infiltrated or evaporated on average 66 % of the runoff flowing into it; unlined systems reduced volumes by 60–92 %.
At Sevogelstrasse the new trees stand in mulch beds where rain from sidewalk and road collects and soaks in.
The shallowest groundwater level over 10 years lies 0.8 m to 20.8 m below ground at Basel's monitoring stations (median 9.8 m).
facts.method: Terrain height minus 10-year maximum level, shallowest per station (81 stations).
facts.caveat: Point values; not interpolated between stations.

facts.claim: ≈ Where groundwater can come within a metre or two of the surface (near the Birs), infiltration needs care; at most stations there are many metres of room.

interventions.name: Open the kerb
interventions.what: A gap in the kerb lets road runoff flow into a rain garden or tree trench instead of the gully.

facts.claim: Inlet design decides whether it works: small slope differences let low flows bypass the opening, and litter, leaves and sediment can block it.

source.label: NACTO Urban Street Stormwater Guide: inlet design

facts.claim: Curb cuts are breaks along a curb that let water flow into a planted bed.

interventions.name: Keep gullies clear
interventions.what: Leaves, litter and sand in gullies and inlets cause much of the local flooding; cleaning is a sponge action too.

facts.claim: In 12,000 resident flood reports from Haarlem and Breda, 70 % of the problems were caused by blocked gully pots, not by too little pipe capacity. Over ten years their damage equalled that of a once-in-a-century flood.
Modelling showed clogged grated inlets capture about 7 % less water when mildly clogged and nearly 50 % less when severely clogged.

source.label: Universidad de Zaragoza: impact of grated inlet clogging on urban pluvial flooding

interventions.name: Green roof
interventions.what: A thin planted layer on a flat roof holds back and evaporates part of the rain.

facts.claim: In Basel-Stadt, flat roofs of 10 m² and more must be greened when built or renovated (§ 72 BPG), with at least 15 cm of regional soil and 20 cm on a third of the roof.
Extensive green roofs in Southern Ontario retain 60–70 % of rain in the warm season and about 50 % over a full year; a roof in Syracuse retained 56 % over 21 months.
facts.caveat: North American climates; most is retained in small storms, much less in long heavy rain.

interventions.name: Roof garden
interventions.what: Deeper substrate where the structure allows: more water held, more evaporation, more use.

facts.claim: Depending on the building structure, thicker substrate can be used and roofs planted as gardens; the more intensive greening holds back and evaporates more water, helping to cool in summer. Semi-intensive and intensive roofs also need watering.

interventions.name: Rain barrel or cistern
interventions.what: Collect roof water at the downpipe for watering; it only helps in a storm if it is empty before the rain.

facts.claim: A household study found people rarely empty their rain barrels, and a full barrel does nothing in a storm; a slow-release valve that drains it over 24 hours was proposed.

source.label: Insurance Bureau of Canada, Wingham rain barrel study (2012)

facts.claim: A modelling study estimated 87 % annual retention for a green roof that re-used water from a cistern, against 43 % for the green roof alone.

source.label: STEP LID guide: green roofs (Florida study)

interventions.name: Disconnect the downpipe
interventions.what: Lead roof water into a garden or bed instead of the sewer.

facts.claim: Portland (Oregon) disconnected more than 50,000 downspouts since 1995, removing over 1.2 billion gallons (about 4.5 million m³) of stormwater a year from its combined sewer.

source.label: City of Portland, Downspout Disconnection Program record

facts.caveat: Program figures as reported by the city.

interventions.name: Water square
interventions.what: A public square that is a place to sit and play when dry and a temporary storage basin in heavy rain.

facts.claim: Rotterdam's Benthemplein water square can store about 1,800 m³ of rainwater.

interventions.name: Dig once
interventions.what: When a street is opened anyway for pipes, heating or tracks, rebuild it as a sponge street in the same works.

facts.claim: Basel uses the district-heating build-out (about 60 km more by 2037) to redesign streets for a better climate: heat protection on about 30 streets so far, with new trees, green areas and unsealing.
55 % of Basel's district-heating projects hold potential for unsealing and greening.
Basel's public-ground permits name utility, sewer, heating, water, gas, electricity or house-connection works in 7,032 construction-site and excavation permits; 334 of them end after 3 October 2026.
facts.caveat: Permits show activity, not the network.

facts.claim: ≈ Each upcoming permit is a window: the street is open anyway, so a tree trench or unsealing costs less than on its own.
